<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par72 />''{{hyphenated word end|secutive|consecutive}}'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=4|verse=39}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=30|verse=1|hidebook=1}}, as well as before the afformatives {{GHGheb|text=תֶם}} and {{GHGheb|text=תֶן}} or before suffixes, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=22|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=6|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=8|verse=34}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=34|verse=4}}. For in all these cases the tone is removed from the {{GHGheb|text=וֹ}} to the following syllable, and this forward movement of the tone produces at the same time a weakening of the ''î'' to ''ē''; thus {{GHGheb|text=הֵקִים}}, {{GHGheb|text=הֲקִימ֫וֹתָ}} (or {{GHGheb|text=הֱק׳}}; on {{GHGheb|text=הַֽעֵדֹ֫תָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=19|verse=23}}, cf. x), but {{GHGheb|text=וַֽהֲקֵֽמֹתָ}}, &c., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=26|verse=30}}, &c.; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=4|verse=39}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=18|verse=26}} (cf., however, {{GHGheb|text=וַֽהֲקֵמֹנ֫וּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=5|verse=4}}). In the same way in the 1st ''pers. sing.'' of the {{GHGterm|perfect Niphʿal}}, the ''ô'' before the separating vowel is always modified to ''û'' ({{GHGheb|text=נְקוּמ֫וֹתִ׳}}); cf. v. In the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} and {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} the separating vowel {{GHGheb|text=־ֶי}} always bears the tone ({{GHGheb|text=תְּקוּמֶ֫ינָה}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|k}}
Without the separating vowel and consequently with the tone-long ''ō'' and ''ē'' instead of ''û'' and ''î'' we find in {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} {{GHGheb|text=תָּבֹ֫אנָה}} (see {{GHGpar|76|g}}); {{GHGheb|text=תָּשֹׁ֫בְןָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=55}} (also {{GHGheb|text=תְּשׁוּבֶ֫ינָה}} in the same verse); {{GHGheb|text=וַתָּשֹׁ֫בְנָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=7|verse=14}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=35|verse=9}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}; on the {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}} {{GHGheb|text=תֵּישַׁ֫בְנָה}} cf. above, note on {{GHGpar|69|b}}); {{GHGheb|text=וַתָּאֹ֫רְנָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=27}}, from {{GHGheb|text=אוֹר}} ({{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}} {{GHGheb|text=וַתִּרְאֶ֫נָה|translate=and they saw}}, see {{GHGpar|75|w}}); in {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הֵנַ֫פְתָּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=20|verse=25}}, also {{GHGheb|text=הֲנִיפ֫וֹתִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=31|verse=21}}; {{GHGheb|text=וְהֵֽטַלְתִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=22|verse=26}}; {{GHGheb|text=תָּשֵׁ֫בְנָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=20|verse=10}}; with a separating vowel, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תְּבִיאֶ֫ינָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv.|chapter=7|verse=30}} from {{GHGheb|text=בּוֹא}}. {{GHGterm|S<sup>e</sup>ghôl}} without {{GHGheb|text=י}} occurs in the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} in {{GHGheb|text=תְּמוּתֶ֫נָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=13|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=1|verse=17}}; and in {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=2|verse=12}}: the Dageš in the ''Nûn'' is, with Baer, to be rejected in all three cases according to the best authorities. Wholly abnormal is {{GHGheb|text=תָּקִ֫ימְנָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=44|verse=25}}, probably an erroneous transposition of {{GHGheb|text=ימ‍}} (for {{GHGheb|text=תְּקִמֶ֫ינָה}}), unless it originates from an incorrect spelling {{GHGheb|text=תָּקֵ֫ימְנָה}} or {{GHGheb|text=תְּקִימֶ֫נָה}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|l}}
'''6.''' The tone, as in verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}} (cf. {{GHGpar|67|k}}), is also generally retained on the stem-syllable in verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}} before the afformatives {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}}, {{GHGheb|text=וּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=־ִי}}; thus {{GHGheb|text=קָ֫מָה}} (but also {{GHGheb|text=בָּזָ֫ה לְךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=19|verse=21}}, probably for the sake of rhythmical uniformity with the following {{GHGheb|text=לָֽעֲגָה לְךָ}}; after {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}} {{GHGheb|text=וְשָׁבָ֫ה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=23|verse=17}}); {{GHGheb|text=קָ֫מוּ}} (but also {{GHGheb|text=קָמ֫וּ}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=28|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=29|verse=9|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=3|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=76|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=5|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=4|verse=18}}; {{GHGheb|text=וְרָצ֫וּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=8|verse=11}}; so especially before a following {{GHGheb|text=א}}, cf. {{GHGpar|49|l}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=13|verse=32}}; {{GHGheb|text=וְנָע֫וּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=19|verse=1}}; before {{GHGheb|text=ע}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=131|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=30|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=4|verse=14}}); {{GHGheb|text=תָּק֫וּמִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָק֫וּמוּ}}, but before a ''suffix'' or with ''Nûn paragogic'' {{GHGheb|text=וַיְסֻכ֫וּם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=28|verse=15}}; {{GHGheb|text=יְקוּמ֫וּן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=33|verse=11}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|m}}
'''7.''' The formation of the conjugations {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}}, {{GHGterm|Puʿal}}, and {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} is, strictly speaking, excluded by the nature of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״וּ}}. It is only in the latest books that we begin to find a few secondary formations, probably borrowed from Aramaic, on the analogy of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ו}} (with consonantal {{GHGheb|text=ו}}, see below, gg); e.g. the {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=עִוֵּד|translate=to surround}}, only in {{GHGheb|text=עִוְּדֻ֫נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=119|verse=61}}; and with change of {{GHGheb|text=ו}} to {{GHGheb|text=י}}, {{GHGheb|text=קִיַּם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=9|verse=31}}, {{GHGheb|text=קִיְּמוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=9|verse=27}}, {{GHGterm|impf.}} {{GHGheb|text=וָאֲֽקַיֵ֫מָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=119|verse=106}}, ''infin.'' {{GHGheb|text=קַיֵּם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=13|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ru|chapter=4|verse=7}} &c., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=9|verse=21}} &c., ''imperat.'' {{GHGheb|text=קַיְּמֵ֫נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=119|verse=28}}; {{GHGheb|text=וְחִיַּכְתֶּם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=1|verse=10}} from {{GHGheb|text=חוּב|translate=to be guilty}}. The {{GHGterm|Hithpaʿēl}} {{GHGheb|text=הִצְטַיֵּד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=9|verse=12}}, which belongs to the older language, is probably a denominative from {{GHGheb|text=צַ֫יִד}}. On the other hand the otherwise less common conjugation ''Pôlēl'' (see {{GHGpar|55|c}}), with its passive and reflexive, is usually<section end=par72 /><noinclude>
